territorial_scope.description: Applies across the EU to intermediary services offered to recipients in the Union, including by providers established outside the Union.

evidence.quote: This Regulation shall apply to intermediary services offered to recipients of the service that have their place of establishment or are located in the Union, irrespective of where the providers of those intermediary services have their place of establishment.

summary.short: EU Regulation 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act) sets harmonised due diligence and liability rules for intermediary services offered to users in the Union, regardless of provider establishment. It imposes tiered duties on hosting services, online platforms and very large online platforms, including notice-and-action, transparency, ad disclosure and risk-assessment obligations.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2022/2065 (Digital Services Act) aims to contribute to the functioning of the internal market for intermediary services by setting harmonised rules for a safe, predictable and trusted online environment (Art. 1). Article 2 applies it to intermediary services offered to recipients in the Union, irrespective of where providers are established, and excludes services that are not intermediary services. It carries forward conditional liability exemptions for mere conduit, caching and hosting services. Due diligence duties are tiered: basic duties for all intermediary services, added duties for hosting services (notice and action, statements of reasons), further duties for online platforms (internal complaint handling, out-of-court dispute settlement, trusted flaggers, trader traceability, limits on dark patterns, and limits on profiling-based advertising using special-category data or targeting minors), and the strongest duties for very large online platforms and search engines above 45 million average monthly active recipients (systemic risk assessment and mitigation, independent audits, researcher data access, a compliance function and a supervisory fee). Member States designate Digital Services Coordinators, and the Commission holds exclusive powers over systemic-risk obligations. The recitals refer to fines and periodic penalty payments. The supplied text covers the recitals and Chapter I only; the operative provisions on these duties, and the application dates, are not in this part.

‘recipient of the service’ means any natural or legal person who uses an intermediary service, in particular for the purposes of seeking information or making it accessible
‘consumer’ means any natural person who is acting for purposes which are outside his or her trade, business, craft, or profession

definitions.term: to offer services in the Union

evidence.quote: ‘to offer services in the Union’ means enabling natural or legal persons in one or more Member States to use the services of a provider of intermediary services that has a substantial connection to the Union
‘substantial connection to the Union’ means a connection of a provider of intermediary services with the Union resulting either from its establishment in the Union or from specific factual criteria
‘distance contract’ means ‘distance contract’ as defined in Article 2, point (7), of Directive 2011/83/EU

‘trader’ means any natural person, or any legal person irrespective of whether it is privately or publicly owned, who is acting, including through any person acting in his or her name or on his or her behalf, for purposes relating to his or her trade, business, craft or profession
‘intermediary service’ means one of the following information society services
a ‘mere conduit’ service, consisting of the transmission in a communication network of information provided by a recipient of the service, or the provision of access to a communication network
a ‘caching’ service, consisting of the transmission in a communication network of information provided by a recipient of the service
a ‘hosting’ service, consisting of the storage of information provided by, and at the request of, a recipient of the service
‘illegal content’ means any information that, in itself or in relation to an activity, including the sale of products or the provision of services, is not in compliance with Union law
‘online platform’ means a hosting service that, at the request of a recipient of the service, stores and disseminates information to the public
‘online search engine’ means an intermediary service that allows users to input queries in order to perform searches of, in principle, all websites, or all websites in a particular language
‘dissemination to the public’ means making information available, at the request of the recipient of the service who provided the information, to a potentially unlimited number of third parties
